subject: VAPA
title: Visual & Performing Arts 7
description: A rotating arts course covering visual art (drawing, color, printmaking, sculpture), music (notation, listening, ukulele or keyboard performance, composition), theatre (improvisation, scene work, a short play) and media arts (photography and stop-motion animation). Projects connect to the medieval and early-modern cultures studied in history, and students keep a sketchbook/process journal and finish with a family exhibition and performance.
framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools (Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Media Arts); 2020 CA Arts Framework

standards.VA:Cr1.1.7: Apply methods to overcome creative blocks.
standards.VA:Cr1.2.7: Develop criteria to guide making a work of art or design to meet an identified goal.
standards.VA:Cr2.1.7: Demonstrate persistence in developing skills with various materials, methods and approaches in creating works of art or design.
standards.VA:Cr2.2.7: Demonstrate awareness of ethical responsibility to oneself and others when posting and sharing content online.
standards.VA:Cr2.3.7: Apply visual organizational strategies to design and produce a work of art, design or media that clearly communicates information or ideas.
standards.VA:Cr3.1.7: Reflect on and explain important information about personal artwork in an artist statement or another format.
standards.VA:Pr4.1.7: Compare and contrast how technologies have changed the way artwork is preserved, presented and experienced.
standards.VA:Pr5.1.7: Based on criteria, analyze and evaluate methods for preparing and presenting art.
standards.VA:Pr6.1.7: Compare and contrast viewing and experiencing collections and exhibitions in different venues.
standards.VA:Re7.1.7: Explain how the method of display, the location and the experience of an artwork influence how it is perceived and valued.
standards.VA:Re7.2.7: Analyze multiple ways that images influence specific audiences.
standards.VA:Re8.1.7: Interpret art by analyzing art-making approaches, the characteristics of form and structure, relevant contextual information, subject matter and use of media to identify ideas and mood conveyed.
standards.VA:Re9.1.7: Compare and explain the difference between an evaluation of an artwork based on personal criteria and one based on a set of established criteria.
standards.VA:Cn10.1.7: Individually or collaboratively create art that reflects ideas and values from various cultures or time periods.
standards.VA:Cn11.1.7: Analyze how response to art is influenced by understanding the time and place in which it was created.
standards.MU:Cr1.1.7: Generate rhythmic, melodic and harmonic phrases and variations over harmonic accompaniments within expanded forms.
standards.MU:Cr2.1.7: Select, organize and document personal musical ideas for arrangements, songs and compositions within expanded forms.
standards.MU:Cr3.1.7: Evaluate their own work, applying selected criteria such as appropriate application of elements of music, including style, form and use of sound sources.
standards.MU:Cr3.2.7: Present the final version of their documented personal composition, song or arrangement, demonstrating unity and variety.
standards.MU:Pr4.2.7: When analyzing selected music, read and identify by name or function standard symbols for rhythm, pitch, articulation, dynamics, tempo and form.
standards.MU:Pr4.3.7: Perform contrasting pieces of music, demonstrating as well as explaining how the music's intent is conveyed by interpretation of the elements of music.
standards.MU:Pr5.1.7: Identify and apply collaboratively developed criteria to rehearse, refine and determine when a piece is ready to perform.
standards.MU:Pr6.1.7: Perform music with technical accuracy and stylistic expression to convey the creator's intent.
standards.MU:Re7.2.7: Classify and explain how the elements of music and expressive qualities relate to the structure of contrasting pieces.
standards.MU:Re8.1.7: Describe a personal interpretation of contrasting works and explain how creators' and performers' application of the elements of music convey expressive intent.
standards.MU:Re9.1.7: Select from teacher-provided criteria to evaluate musical works or performances.
standards.MU:Cn11.0.7: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts and daily life.
standards.TH:Cr1.1.7: Investigate multiple perspectives and solutions to staging problems in a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cr2.1.7: Examine and justify original ideas and artistic choices in a drama/theatre work based on critical analysis, background knowledge and historical and cultural context.
standards.TH:Cr3.1.7: Demonstrate focus and concentration in the rehearsal process to analyze and refine choices in a devised or scripted drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Pr4.1.7: Consider multiple planned technical elements during the rehearsal process for a devised or scripted drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Pr5.1.7: Participate in a variety of acting exercises and techniques that can be applied in a rehearsal or drama/theatre performance.
standards.TH:Pr6.1.7: Participate in rehearsals for a drama/theatre work that will be shared with an audience.
standards.TH:Re7.1.7: Compare recurring patterns in drama/theatre works.
standards.TH:Re8.1.7: Identify the artistic choices made in a drama/theatre work through participation and observation.
standards.TH:Re9.1.7: Explain preferences, using supporting evidence and criteria, to evaluate drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cn11.2.7: Research and discuss how a playwright might have intended a drama/theatre work to be produced.
standards.MA:Cr1.1.7: Generate ideas, goals and solutions for original media artworks through application of chosen generative methods.
standards.MA:Cr2.1.7: Design, propose and evaluate artistic ideas, plans, prototypes and production processes for media arts productions.
standards.MA:Cr3.1.7: Coordinate production processes to integrate content and stylistic conventions for determined purpose and meaning in media arts productions.
standards.MA:Pr5.1.7: Exhibit an increasing set of artistic, design, technical and soft skills through performing various roles in producing media artworks.
standards.MA:Pr6.1.7: Evaluate various presentation formats in order to fulfill various tasks and defined processes in the presentation and distribution of media artworks.
standards.MA:Re7.1.7: Describe, compare and analyze the qualities of and relationships between the components and style in media artworks.
standards.MA:Cn10.1.7: Access, evaluate and integrate personal and external resources to inform the creation of original media artworks.

units.title: Drawing Foundations
units.big_idea: Careful observation, value and perspective let artists create the illusion of form and space.

units.title: Color and Painting
units.big_idea: Color relationships and composition communicate mood and meaning.

units.title: Music Literacy and Listening
units.big_idea: Reading notation and listening analytically reveal how composers structure music.

units.title: Music Performance and Composition
units.big_idea: Musicians rehearse with criteria and compose with unity and variety.

units.title: Printmaking and Art Across Cultures
units.big_idea: Artists across times and cultures—Islamic, Japanese, medieval European—use pattern, line and printmaking to share ideas.

units.title: Theatre: From Improv to Performance
units.big_idea: Actors use voice, body and focused rehearsal to bring scripts to life for an audience.

units.title: Media Arts: Photography and Animation
units.big_idea: Media artists plan, capture and edit images and motion to tell stories responsibly.

units.title: Sculpture and Exhibition
units.big_idea: Three-dimensional form and thoughtful presentation complete an artist's year of work.

days.title: Sketchbook setup
days.work: Design a sketchbook cover and fill one page with 20 different kinds of lines.

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Draw your non-dominant hand in blind contour three times for 3 minutes each.

days.title: Modified contour
days.work: Draw a shoe in modified contour, glancing at the paper only at corners.

days.title: Beating creative block
days.work: Try three idea-starters (random object, word prompt, 'draw it 5 ways') and fill a page.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Choose your best contour drawing and write three sentences about line quality.

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Create a 9-step value scale with pencil and a second using hatching and cross-hatching.

days.title: Shading spheres
days.work: Draw and shade three spheres with highlight, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow.

days.title: Egg study
days.work: Light an egg with a lamp and draw it realistically for 25 minutes.

days.title: Texture shading
days.work: Shade a crumpled paper bag using varied pencil grades.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare your egg study to a Renaissance drawing and note one technique to improve.

weeks.assessment: Value scale and shaded egg study.

objectives: Draw in one- and two-point perspective
materials: print of Raphael's School of Athens

days.title: One-point
days.work: Draw block letters of your initials in one-point perspective.

days.title: Finding vanishing points
days.work: Find and trace orthogonals in The School of Athens to locate its vanishing point.

days.title: One-point room
days.work: Draw your bedroom or a hallway in one-point perspective.

days.title: Two-point
days.work: Draw a street corner of buildings in two-point perspective.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Explain in writing how perspective changed art in the Renaissance.

days.title: Face proportions
days.work: Learn standard face proportions and draw a guideline face.

days.title: Features
days.work: Practice drawing eyes, nose and mouth from a mirror, one page each.

days.title: Self-portrait sketch
days.work: Sketch a self-portrait from a mirror using guidelines.

days.title: Self-portrait shading
days.work: Add value to the self-portrait using the light source.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare the self-portrait to an early-year sketch and list improvements.

weeks.topic: Still life composition and artist statement
objectives: Compose and render a still life

days.title: Arranging
days.work: Arrange 4–5 objects and use a paper viewfinder to make three thumbnail compositions.

days.title: Drawing
days.work: Draw the strongest composition lightly with accurate proportion and overlap.

days.title: Shading
days.work: Shade the still life fully with a range of values.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Analyze a Dutch still life (e.g., Claesz) and compare its composition to yours.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a 150-word artist statement explaining your choices.

weeks.assessment: Still life drawing and artist statement (rubric).

materials: tempera or acrylic paint (red, yellow, blue, white, black)

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Mix and paint a 12-part color wheel from primaries only.

days.title: Tints and shades
days.work: Paint tint and shade scales for two colors.

days.title: Color schemes
days.work: Paint four small squares showing complementary, analogous, monochromatic and triadic schemes.

days.title: Neutrals
days.work: Mix browns and grays by combining complements.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Label your swatches and quiz yourself on color vocabulary.

materials: images of Van Gogh and Picasso Blue Period works

days.title: Analyze mood
days.work: Compare Van Gogh's 'Starry Night' and Picasso's 'The Old Guitarist' and describe how color creates mood.

days.title: Same scene, two moods
days.work: Paint the same simple landscape twice, once warm and once cool.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a personal place and sketch three thumbnails for a landscape painting.

days.title: Set criteria
days.work: Write criteria for the painting (color scheme, focal point, depth).

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Discuss which thumbnail best meets the criteria and why.

days.title: Underpainting
days.work: Block in background, middle ground and foreground with a thin underpainting.

days.title: Background
days.work: Paint the sky and distant areas lighter and cooler for atmospheric perspective.

days.title: Middle ground
days.work: Paint the middle ground with more detail and saturation.

days.title: Foreground
days.work: Paint the foreground with the most detail and contrast.

days.title: Details
days.work: Add final details and sign the painting.

objectives: Critique with personal vs. established criteria

days.title: Feldman critique
days.work: Use the describe-analyze-interpret-judge method to critique a famous landscape.

days.title: Self-critique
days.work: Critique your own painting with both personal and established criteria and note differences.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Make one revision to strengthen the focal point.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write an artist statement for the painting.

days.title: Mini show
days.work: Display drawings and painting for family and explain one choice in each.

objectives: Read rhythms with whole through sixteenth notes

days.title: Note values
days.work: Complete musictheory.net lessons on note and rest durations and clap 8 rhythms.

days.title: Time signatures
days.work: Identify meter in 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 excerpts and conduct each pattern.

days.title: Sixteenth notes
days.work: Count and clap sixteenth-note rhythms with 1-e-and-a syllables.

days.title: Bucket drumming
days.work: Perform a 16-bar bucket drumming rhythm with a metronome.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a rhythm-reading quiz on musictheory.net exercises.

objectives: Read notes on treble and bass clef

days.title: Treble clef
days.work: Learn treble clef note names and complete a note-naming drill.

days.title: Bass clef
days.work: Learn bass clef note names and complete a drill.

days.title: Keyboard
days.work: Locate notes on a keyboard and play C, G and F major scales.

days.title: Steps
days.work: Build major scales using the whole-whole-half pattern.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a note-reading and scale quiz.

materials: recordings of Hildegard von Bingen, a troubadour song, Palestrina and a madrigal

days.title: Chant
days.work: Listen to Gregorian chant and Hildegard von Bingen and describe texture and melody.

days.title: Polyphony
days.work: Listen to a Palestrina mass movement and identify the interweaving voices.

days.title: Secular music
days.work: Listen to a troubadour song and an English madrigal and compare to sacred music.

days.title: Global connections
days.work: Listen to Japanese gagaku and West African kora music and compare to European music of the same era.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a listening log comparing three pieces using musical vocabulary.

objectives: Identify forms (AB, ABA, rondo, theme and variations)
materials: recordings of Mozart 'Twinkle' variations, Beethoven 'Für Elise'

days.title: Dynamics and tempo
days.work: Learn Italian dynamic and tempo terms and mark them while listening to a piece.

days.title: Rondo
days.work: Map the form of 'Für Elise' (ABACA) with colored blocks.

days.title: Variations
days.work: Listen to Mozart's 'Twelve Variations on Ah vous dirai-je, Maman' and describe how each variation changes.

days.title: Interpretation
days.work: Compare two performances of the same piece and explain how performers' choices change expression.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a form and expression quiz.

days.title: Triads
days.work: Build C, F and G major triads on keyboard or ukulele.

days.title: Major vs minor
days.work: Play major and minor triads and describe the difference in sound.

days.title: I-IV-V
days.work: Play a I-IV-V-I progression and identify it in a 12-bar blues recording.

days.title: Song chords
days.work: Strum or play chords to a simple folk song like 'This Land Is Your Land'.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a chord identification quiz by ear and on paper.

days.title: Strumming patterns
days.work: Learn down-down-up-up-down-up strumming and play it on C and Am.

days.title: Chord changes
days.work: Practice C-Am-F-G changes with a metronome at 60 bpm.

days.title: Song 1
days.work: Learn the verse of a chosen song with the four chords.

days.title: Song 2
days.work: Learn a contrasting song (minor key or different tempo).

days.title: Check
days.work: Record yourself playing and set practice goals with criteria.

materials: Chrome Music Lab Song Maker or notation app (MuseScore)

days.title: Motifs
days.work: Create three 2-bar motifs using Song Maker and choose the strongest.

days.title: Phrases
days.work: Extend the motif into a 4-bar question phrase and 4-bar answer phrase.

days.title: Cadences
days.work: End the melody on the tonic for a strong cadence and test alternatives.

days.title: Notation
days.work: Notate the 8-bar melody with rhythm and dynamics.

days.title: Self-evaluate
days.work: Evaluate the melody using criteria of unity and variety and revise one bar.

objectives: Add harmony and form to a composition

days.title: Harmonize
days.work: Add I-IV-V chords under the melody.

days.title: B section
days.work: Compose a contrasting 8-bar B section to create ABA form.

days.title: Arrange
days.work: Add a rhythm part or bass line.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse performing the composition and the two songs, using a criteria checklist.

days.title: Peer feedback
days.work: Play the composition for a family member and record their feedback.

days.title: Final rehearsal
days.work: Run the full recital program twice and fix problem spots.

days.title: Program
days.work: Design a recital program with titles and short program notes.

days.title: Recital
days.work: Perform two contrasting songs and the original composition for family.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Watch the recording and evaluate with a performance rubric.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on growth as a musician this semester.

days.title: Context
days.work: View Alhambra and mosque tilework and discuss why geometric patterns are central in Islamic art.

days.title: Construction
days.work: Construct an 8-point star pattern with compass and ruler.

days.title: Repeat
days.work: Extend the pattern into a repeating tile grid.

days.title: Color
days.work: Color the pattern with a planned color scheme.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write how understanding the culture changes how you see the pattern.

objectives: Carve and print a relief block

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a print inspired by Japanese woodblock prints (Hokusai) with strong positive and negative space.

days.title: Transfer and carve
days.work: Transfer the design onto a foam plate and incise lines.

days.title: First prints
days.work: Ink with a brayer and pull test prints, adjusting pressure.

days.title: Edition
days.work: Pull an edition of 4 prints, numbering and signing each.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare your print process to Hokusai's 'The Great Wave' production.

days.title: Manuscripts
days.work: Study images of the Book of Kells and a Persian manuscript and compare them.

days.title: Calligraphy
days.work: Practice a gothic or italic alphabet with a chisel-tip marker.

days.title: Illuminated letter
days.work: Design an illuminated initial with border decoration.

days.title: Finish page
days.work: Write a short quote in calligraphy and add metallic accents.

days.title: Preservation
days.work: Compare how manuscripts were preserved then and how museums digitize art now.

objectives: Analyze art from Mesoamerica and West Africa
materials: images of Aztec codices and adinkra symbols

days.title: Codex art
days.work: Analyze Aztec codex images for color, line and storytelling.

days.title: Adinkra
days.work: Learn the meanings of 8 West African adinkra symbols.

days.title: Stamp design
days.work: Design a personal symbol and carve it into a potato or foam stamp.

days.title: Printed cloth
days.work: Stamp a repeating pattern on fabric or paper with traditional and personal symbols.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write about respectful inspiration versus copying cultural art.

days.title: Warm-ups
days.work: Do vocal and physical warm-ups (tongue twisters, mirror exercise).

days.title: Yes, and
days.work: Play 'Yes, and' story-building improv with a family member.

days.title: Tableaux
days.work: Create frozen tableaux for scenes from history (e.g., signing Magna Carta).

days.title: Objectives
days.work: Improvise short scenes where each character has a clear objective and obstacle.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Journal on which game built confidence and why.

days.title: Projection
days.work: Practice breath support and projection reading lines across a room.

days.title: Inflection
days.work: Say one line ten ways to express ten different emotions.

days.title: Physical character
days.work: Walk as five different characters, changing posture, tempo and center.

days.title: Stage directions
days.work: Learn stage areas (upstage, downstage left, etc.) and follow blocking commands.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a 1-minute monologue from A Midsummer Night's Dream with clear diction.

objectives: Analyze a script for character and staging
materials: short play script (e.g., a public-domain one-act or the Pyramus and Thisbe scene)

days.title: Read the script
days.work: Read a short one-act (e.g., the Pyramus and Thisbe scene) and summarize plot and characters.

days.title: Playwright intent
days.work: Research how the play was originally staged and discuss the playwright's intentions.

days.title: Character analysis
days.work: Write a character profile with objectives and subtext for your role.

days.title: Design plan
days.work: Sketch set, costume and prop designs using household materials.

days.title: Patterns
days.work: Compare comic patterns in this play with a sitcom episode.

days.title: Read-through
days.work: Hold a read-through with family members playing roles.

days.title: Blocking
days.work: Block the scene and write blocking notes in the script.

days.title: Memorize
days.work: Work toward off-book with cue-line drills.

days.title: Run-through
days.work: Run the full scene with props and give notes.

days.title: Tech
days.work: Add costumes, sound effects or lighting cues and run again.

materials: recorded play or local theatre performance

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Hold a full dress rehearsal.

days.title: Performance
days.work: Perform the play for family or a homeschool group.

days.title: Watch a production
days.work: Watch a filmed or local live theatre production.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Write a review of the production with evidence about acting, design and directing choices.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your own performance and the artistic choices you made.

days.title: Analyze photos
days.work: Analyze Dorothea Lange's 'Migrant Mother' and a modern ad for composition and audience influence.

days.title: Rule of thirds
days.work: Take 10 photos using the rule of thirds.

days.title: Lines and framing
days.work: Take 10 photos using leading lines and natural frames.

days.title: Angles
days.work: Photograph one object from 5 angles (bird's-eye, worm's-eye, etc.) and compare effect.

days.title: Select
days.work: Choose your best 5 photos and caption each with the technique used.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a 6–8 photo essay about a day in your family or neighborhood.

days.title: Shoot
days.work: Take photos for the essay, asking permission before photographing people.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Crop and adjust exposure in a free photo editor.

days.title: Ethics
days.work: Learn about copyright, Creative Commons and consent, and write sharing rules for your work.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the photo essay as a slideshow with captions.

days.title: Study
days.work: Watch short clips of stop-motion and analyze how frames create motion.

days.title: Test
days.work: Make a 2-second test animation of a ball bouncing at 12 frames per second.

days.title: Storyboard
days.work: Storyboard a 30-second story with beginning, middle and end.

days.title: Characters
days.work: Build characters from clay or LEGO.

days.title: Set
days.work: Build a set and plan lighting to avoid flicker.

days.title: Shoot scene 1
days.work: Capture frames for the first scene of the animation.

days.title: Shoot scenes 2–3
days.work: Capture frames for remaining scenes.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit timing and add titles and credits.

days.title: Sound
days.work: Add a soundtrack or sound effects, possibly using your own composition.

days.title: Premiere
days.work: Premiere the animation for family and reflect on roles you played in production.

objectives: Build a form using additive methods

days.title: Sculpture study
days.work: Compare Donatello's 'David' and Michelangelo's 'David' from multiple viewpoints online.

days.title: Armature
days.work: Build a foil and wire armature for a small figure or animal.

days.title: Clay
days.work: Add clay over the armature, building major forms.

days.title: Detail
days.work: Add texture and detail with tools.

days.title: Dry
days.work: Smooth and let the sculpture dry; sketch it from three views.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Sketch a design for a soap carving from three views.

days.title: Carve
days.work: Rough-carve the soap block with a plastic knife.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Refine details and smooth surfaces.

days.title: Finish clay piece
days.work: Paint and seal the clay sculpture.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write an artist statement for one sculpture.

weeks.assessment: Soap carving and finished clay sculpture.

objectives: Select and prepare work for exhibition

days.title: Virtual museum
days.work: Take a Google Arts & Culture virtual tour and note how works are displayed and labeled.

days.title: Select
days.work: Select 8–10 works representing each unit.

days.title: Prepare
days.work: Mat or mount 2-D work and create pedestals for sculptures.

days.title: Labels
days.work: Write museum-style labels for each piece.

days.title: Layout
days.work: Plan the exhibition layout in a room.

days.title: Install
days.work: Install the exhibition in the home or community space.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a song, monologue and gallery talk for showcase night.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Host the arts showcase: gallery, music performance and animation screening.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Collect visitor comments on response cards.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare viewing art at home versus a museum and how location changes value.

days.title: Before & after
days.work: Compare first and last drawings of the year and list three skills that improved.

days.title: Digital portfolio
days.work: Photograph all work and create a digital portfolio slideshow.

days.title: Free choice
days.work: Create one free-choice artwork in your favorite medium.

days.title: Reflection letter
days.work: Write a letter to your future self about your artistic identity.

days.title: Goals
days.work: Set goals for VAPA 8 and choose a summer sketchbook challenge.
